teamMessage.title: A Word From Our Team
teamMessage.description:
Plantiful started as a high-school experiment that blossomed into something much bigger. None of us had built a mobile app before and, honestly, we barely knew anything about plants. We learned everything on the fly and we're proud of what we created. Every good story ends eventually, so we closed this chapter by open-sourcing the product, documentation, and design system—letting anyone continue the journey, learn from our mistakes, or keep building on the vision.

You still won't find Plantiful in the App Store or on Google Play. Thanks to the open-source code you can try it today, or send us a note for a ready-made demo.

foreword.title: RedHat Summer Camp
foreword.description: Plantiful was born during Red Hat Summer Camp 2022, where a series of workshops guided us toward the final project. Within a few hours we clarified the idea, the pitch, and the deck. The competition was fierce, but we still managed to win.
highlights: Within 48 hours we shaped Plantiful's vision and, with mentor support, built the MVP.
Presented our idea and won Best Project at Red Hat Summer Camp.

links.label: Red Hat Summer Camp 2022 recap
links.description: Red Hat Research recap of the 2022 Brno camp where we first pitched Plantiful.

kyndryl_challenge.title: Kyndryl Challenge
kyndryl_challenge.description: Winning Red Hat motivated us to keep going, so we entered the Kyndryl Challenge and went through another round of hands-on workshops. We doubled down on understanding our audience, completed the project concept, and added even more ideas. The Kyndryl judges loved it, we shared first place with another team, and we were offered a year-long internship to start building the app.
highlights: Presented our vision to the jury.
Won the challenge and earned an internship to keep building Plantiful.

links.label: Kyndryl Challenge recap (CZ)
links.description: School article covering the Kyndryl Challenge finale where Plantiful earned a Kyndryl internship.

kyndryl.title: Kyndryl Internship
kyndryl.description: During the year-long Kyndryl internship we slowly turned the prototype into reality. We brought in a dedicated designer, Honza Truneček, who played a key role in shaping the visual identity. We designed the final look and features of the app, worked as a team, prepared for more competitions, kept developing the product, and consulted everything with our project manager from Kyndryl.
highlights: Designed the final look and feature set of the app.
Worked as a team, prepared for more competitions, and continued building the product.

ja_expo.title: JA Expo
ja_expo.description:
We had already validated the technical side of the app and were actively building it. At the last minute we received an invitation to JA EXPO, and within a month we had to prepare the annual report, business model, and monetisation plan. In Prague's Harfa Gallery we presented Plantiful to thousands of visitors and collected feedback from them as well as from the category judges.

We won Best Business Pitch and finished second in the STEM category.
highlights: Collected feedback from more than 2,000 visitors during live demos.
Made the TOP 10 finals by winning Best Business Pitch.

links.label: JA Expo recap (CZ)
links.description: School article about JA Expo 2023 where Plantiful won Best Business Pitch and 2nd place in STEM.

fekt_eeict.title: FEKT EEICT
fekt_eeict.description:
Another stop on the journey was the high-school track of the VUT FEKT EEICT conference. It became our biggest challenge yet—the field was stacked with great teams. We had to write a technical paper, document the algorithms, explain how we implemented the Plant.id API, and describe the entire technology stack behind the app.

A jury of academics and industry mentors awarded us third place, and their feedback helped us polish the last bugs before release.
highlights: Won 3rd place in the EEICT 2024 high-school track.
Wrote a technical whitepaper outlining the app's architecture.

release.title: Open-source Release
release.description: We spent months debating what comes next. Without outside investment we couldn't compete with international teams that can burn millions before the first revenue, so we decided to give everything back to the community—completely free. Anyone can use our app as a template, learn from our mistakes, and keep shaping the vision.
highlights: Open-sourced the entire Plantiful codebase and design system.
Documented the full technology stack and implementation.
